title: Using Postpositions with Pronouns vs Nouns

sections.content:
Contrast how postpositions connect to nouns versus personal pronouns:
- With a noun, the noun is in the nominative case and the postposition is uninflected: *a ház előtt* (in front of the house), *a színház mellett* (beside the theater).
- With a pronoun, the postposition takes personal suffixes and the pronoun (*én, te, ő*) is usually omitted: **előttem** (in front of me), **melletted** (next to you). If emphasized, add the pronoun: *Pont énelőttem áll!* (He is standing right in front of ME!).

items.spanish: A posta a gyógyszertár mellett van, te meg mellettem állsz.
items.english: The post office is next to the pharmacy, and you are standing next to me.

items.spanish: Nem láttalak, mert pontosan mögöttem álltál a boltban.
items.english: I didn't see you because you stood right behind me in the shop.

items.spanish: Az egész élet előttetek áll még, fiatalok!
items.english: All of life is still ahead of you, youngsters!
